author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will have two batteries established, which, as soon as they are completed, will render the coasting of the coast on, in the sight of the enemy wing."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will visit our most advanced posts on the side of Carnino, Certosa and the heights of the Marta, which were taken to the enemy on the 8th Floreal; after that he will make two maps: 1° One of the heights, which joins the heights of Ponte-di-Nava to Carnino, to Certosa, at the height of the Marta;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I did not write to you, my friend, because I had no good news to give you. You are not kept war commissioner;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received your letter. I have dined today at General Scherer's house with your wife; I will be charmed to be able to be good to her."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "In accordance with the order of the Executive Board of the 12th Ventôse, General Alexandre Berthier is appointed Chief of Staff of the Year of Italy. Warrant Officer General Vignolle remains Deputy Chief of Staff."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Long live the king! 128 ". I suppose that Mr. Moulin's mission as a parliamentarian was relative to frames of Celtic nature, whose thread I seek with stubbornness."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have too good an opinion of you to think that you were going to any end that would be disavowed by the man of honour and would cause blood to flow. You would have been responsible in the eyes of the whole of Europe and your army in particular."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am determined to attack myself. As a result, General Menard departs tonight from Cadibona and Quiliano, with 4,000 men, to give on Montenotte. Generals Joubert and Dommartin leave from Santiago with 5,000 men, to meet with the troops of General Menard."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Take bread for the 14 half-brigade, at the Madonna, where there are, and take, with all your troops, the positions you will think most advantageous to seem to threaten the enemy at Sassello;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Laharpe will send the 14" half brigade and the 2" battalion of the 21" to the orders of General Masséna."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As I believe he has passed through the heights, he may not have arrived; so I direct you to pass the orders, which I ask you to carry out with the greatest punctuality and with your ordinary courage."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Cervoni, who commanded it, under his command 70 and 1)9 half-brigade, supported the fire with the intrepidity that characterizes the soldiers of freedom. I did not change it on the true intentions of the enemies."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "DoI. 10 146 <". He tells him yourself of what you propose to do. It is only a matter of pre-post, but important as a result of our victories."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Brigadier General Menard is ordered to leave, immediately after receiving this order, the position he occupies, to go to the heights near Cairo, on the left bank of the Bormida."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will make sure that the order is established everywhere, and will speed up particularly the evacuation of the artillery, either with horses or with men. After having put everything into operation and having cooperated with General Masséna, he will come to report his mission to the general in chief."
sourceTitle: To General Warrant Officer Vial, Carcare, 1796-04-15
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You must have been ordered to take the intermediate position between Biestro and Rocca-Vignale, to support General Augereau's attack. Please put the greatest accuracy in the execution of your movement."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is ordered that Brigadier General Despinoy leave at one o'clock in the morning to go to Dego, where he will visit all the posts. After having visited General Masséna, he will return to report to the Chief General if we are aware of any movement of the Ençmi."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will see, through the relationship that I send to the Executive Board, the details of the battle of Montenofte and Millesimo. I do not conceal to you that I am not assisted either by genius or by artillery;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I make known to you, General Citizen, the desire that I would have to make, in Sassello, a search that would be useful from several points of view; I would wish that within an hour you would cause the IV half-brigade to go to Savone, via Sassello."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will find there the 84 half-brigade, commanded by General Dommartin, who will come under his command; it would be necessary that he had arrived at two o'clock after noon."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The dispatch of your order, attached to your letter of the 15 Germinal, then of the letter of the Executive Board of the 21st Pluviôse relating to cavalry, convinced me of the zeal that you brought to its execution. Nothing less was expected of your patriotism;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier is ordered to carry himself, with all his division and the four regiments of troops on horseback who must go to bed in Priero, on the right of the enemies."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "These battalions will be followed by the third as soon as it has been raised at the camp cut off by 1,200 men whom General Augei'eau has ordered to send. You will find in Lapre and Lesegno two cannon pieces and four regiments of troops on horseback."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order General Joubert to be returned at two hours after midnight, and to leave as soon as he has been raised, to go to the village of Lesegno."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The two shells that are in battery against Ceva and the four pieces of 4 will also go to Lesegno."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "This is due to the continuation of our successes, and we cannot take too much action to ensure it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Beaumont will order the 7 Hussard regiment and the 15 dragons to leave Lesegno to go to the village of Niella, headquarters of General Masséna, where they will be at his command."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The inhabitants must all work on this operation, so that it is very-promptly completed: otherwise the chief general warns them that he will take the means of rigour to compel them to do so and punish them for neglecting to carry out his orders on this subject."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Accordingly, he ordered: 1" To the General, Chief of Staff, to report to him within twenty-five hours on the moral conduct of the adjutants general and other officers attached to the staff."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have 100,000 men against me, who have only 34,000 infantry and 3,500 cavalry. The enemy has strong positions and a large artillery perfectly equipped;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am sending you a request made by the General with a suspension of arms, and I am attaching to it the answer I have given '. I hope that it will be in accordance with your intentions."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Ciloycn Junot, my aide de camp, will present twenty and half flags taken from the Austrians and the Piedmontese, at the battles of Montenotte, Millesimo, Dego and Mondovi; there are four which are the flags of the bodyguards of the king of Sardinia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I send you. Citizen Minister, twenty-one flags taken to the enemy by the army of Italy. I cannot hide from you how much the counter-order you gave to the light artillery company, which I had sent from Paris to Nice, harms my operations."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am so burdened with fatigue and hard work that I cannot tell you any more. BONAPARTJÎ. My respect to Madame and little Julie-Joseph."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is important that the passage that has just been spoken to him be well guarded, in order to ensure our communication."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached, General, an order to make leave the 14'' half-brigade. If new movements of the enemy, which I do not know, made you judge this unwise departure, you would warn me immediately."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The order was given to him twice', and it is extraordinary that he has not yet complied with it. He had to be raised at the camp cut off from Ceva by Brigadier General Miollis."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General has received, Citizens, your letter of the 5th of this month. He is very persuasive of the good spirit of your fellow citizens and their attachment to the French Republic;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I was told that we should take advice of events in unforeseen circumstances"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I send you, Sir, the order of your king to return the place of Coni to the officer with an order of me. I beg you, therefore, to kindly return the place and the citadel to General Despinoy, bearer of the present."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You know, sir, that the distance from here to one of these two places makes it necessary that the king's order be dispatched tomorrow, so that he may pass the 11th Floreal. A division of my army is already sent to that side."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "They evacuate and pass the Po. I have ordered Augercau to go to Chivesana. If Beaulieu is already in the middle of retreat, send to the meeting of Augercau so that he will take the road of Nizza-delia-Paglia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I write to Laharpe that, if he hears that the enemy is in the midst of retreat, he writes to you, so that you take the way to Nizzadella-Paglia. I will be tomorrow evening in your cantons."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The garrison will go out to the destination indicated to it by the General Commander of the Piedmontese army. General Miollis will seize all posts or forts, and will consult with the ex-Governor to make the garrison leave without delay."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I would also like you to make me pass 4,000 men through the valley of Aosta; I get the passage from the courtyard of Turin."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Augereau is ordered to direct his march on Bistagno, on the Bormida; General Masséna having left Alba this morning with all his division, to go to Nizza-della-Paglia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Augereau is ordered to leave tomorrow morning, with his division, to occupy the villages of Pizzale and Cervesina and those on the edge of Po, between the river of Staffora and that of Coppa;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He shall take care to evacuate the oats removed from the enemies from Tortone; he shall keep watch over the flying bridges which shall be built in front of Sale;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I ordered that 400 prisoners be brought in for the exchange of the 400 that you had the kindness to pass to Cheraseo. The Chief of Staff will send you the state of the officers of your army that the fate of the weapons has taken prisoner."
sourceTitle: To King of Sardinia's Commander-in-Chief, Tortona, 1796-05-04
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general is outraged by the complaints against the banditry and the harassment of all kinds that some men of the 84 half-brigade allow."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I urge you to take care of this important object without delay. I send you Tordre de route to establish for the march of the troops who will join the army and for the men travelling alone."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will find myself too happy, in all circumstances, to be able to give you marks of the esteem and the distinguished consideration with which I am, etc."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Macquart will command in Coni and in the conquered country, from the right bank of the Stura to the Trinità, at the passage of Fossano, following by Sant'-Albano, Consovero, Morozzo, Reinette, Chiusa, Rastello and Prea."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "he will prepare bread, wine and meat for 12,000 men, as well as the necessary fodder for 4,000 horses. He will inquire if there are boats six miles above Plaisance;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Warrant Officer General Vial is ordered to go to the Po Pass, where he will raise Warrant Officer General Franceschi and the deputies who are there. He will place himself next to the flying bridge to get the order there, in order to speed up the passage of the troops."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Kilmaine will give General Beaumont the order to immediately pass the Po, to take command of all the horses that have passed and pass successively."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "If he sees anything else contrary to the good order, he will instruct me on it, so that I may cause it to be repressed. Persons, properties and cults must be respected;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He ordered a body of 0.000 men and 2,000 horses to come to meet us and oppose our landing, or to attack us when we were not yet trained; he was mistaken in his calculation. At midday, I learned that an enemy division was very close to us;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The enemies left 2,000 men in the castle of Milan, which I will necessarily invest. You can count in your calculations as if I were in Milan."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We passed Po, twice beat the enemy, caught or killed 3,000 men in various business, luggage, shops and twenty cannon pieces."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna will hold his division ready to leave tomorrow, at four o'clock in the morning; she will move when Chief General Hii gives the order."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will follow his cartridges. He can also bring in the 300 men I had requested for the guard of the headquarters. The 84® half-brigade will remain in Lodi to do the service of the place."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The commander of the 84'' half-brigade will have the general beat in an hour; he will leave for Crenia, and from there will follow the march of the wing."
sourceTitle: To Chief Of Brigade Rampon, Lodi, 1796-05-12
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He is warned that the 84' half-brigade has been ordered to follow the movements of his division, to which it must be reunited; in the event that it has not yet carried out this order, - he will order him to join him promptly."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received, Sir, the ration of the suspension of arms which you have accepted from the Duke of Parma. I send you General Cervoni, so that you can settle with him all the details of the execution of the said suspension."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We made 300 prisoners and took four cannon pieces. Beaulieu escapes at all legs"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "At the reception of the letter of the Executive Board of the 18th, your intentions were fulfilled, and the Milanese is here for us. I will soon walk, to execute your views, on Livorno and on Rome."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am sending you, Citizens Directors, a letter of exchange of 650,000 pounds banco, addressed to Mr. Deveaux, treasurer of foreign bodies. Perhaps you will find the way to take advantage of it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Your army has returned the Mincio; any resistance you would make would be contrary to the true rights of the war. The city of Milan, which must interest you in so many ways, would be compromised, if you insisted on keeping the fort longer."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will consult with the general Despinoy for the means of transport of these rifles, of which 2,000 are intended to be sent to General Serurier, in Plaisance. The director of the artillery park, in Lodi, will send him this shipment as soon as possible."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "In this regard, he will use all the resources that the country offers, and will work with the war commissioner to place in Tende ox relays that will help to mount the various convoys."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It will keep a diary of the siege. The trench will be raised exactly every twenty-four hours. General Masséna will set the time at which it will be mounted and the place of the appointment where the troops must assemble."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Duke of Parma paid his contribution; he had already paid 500,000 pounds and he was executing for the rest. Faypoult would have wanted nothing to be paid to this prince;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As a result, the supplement of the 3 pounds and 6 pounds per month will cease from the 1st Prairial. General staff officers, war commissioners and health officers of hospitals below the Alps and the Apennine, are included in this provision."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The general in chief of the army instructs me, Sir, to notify you that he accepts the proposal that you make to him to respect the city of Milan and not to commit any hostile act on this side."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 69" half-brigade will remain in Lodi. General Augercau is warned that the auxiliary company of the 19" half-brigade has the order to go to Pavie to keep garrison there."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Soldiers, You have rushed as a torrent from the top of the Apennine; you have hurled, scattered, scattered all that opposed your march."
sourceTitle: To His Brothers In Arms, Milan, 1796-05-20
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will, Citizen, send out without delay for Tortone, escort sounds, trunks, merchandise"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As a result of the decree made by the General in Chief of the Italian Army and the Commissioner of the Executive Director Saliceti, relating to the 20."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General instructs me to warn you that he is dissatisfied with the manner in which the artillery is supplied, and that the orders he has sent to you have been poorly executed."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "When you leave, you will be given 24,000 pounds of money, which you will use to encourage the patriots."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The citizen Balbi, the banker of the Republic, rewarded you 15,000 pounds. You will buy, with this sum, a hundred rifles, (three hundred pairs of pistols, three thousand rifle stones, five to six thousand pounds of powder and eight to ten thousand pounds of lead, which you will hand over to the citizen Bonelli."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna will leave Codogno, with all the troops at his command which are in Lodi, tomorrow 5, at five o'clock of the clever, to go to Offanengo, beyond Crema."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Order to the 20" regiment of dragons and to the 24" hunters to depart from Offanengo to go to Milan with all diligence. Same order to the 2" battalion of the 21° half-brigade."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna will give orders to General Menard to meet with him with all the troops he commands."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I encourage scientists to come together and offer their views on the means or needs they would have to take to give science and fine arts a new life and a new existence."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "A lost multitude, without real means of resistance, carries on to the last excesses in several communes, ignores the Republic and braves the triumphant love of several kings."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Augereau, with all the rest of his division, will leave at 3 o'clock in the morning, tomorrow 9, from the position he occupies, to go to Ponte-San-Marco"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "By order of the General in Chief. Deposit of the Guprre. 501. _ IN GENERAL BERTHIER. Headquarters, Brescia, 8 Prairial to the IV"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1." — Consequently, the general in the branch declares that all villages which have not complied with his order of the 6 Prairial'are beautiful."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order him to go straight to headquarters, and be replaced. Citizen Songis will replace him, pending his arrival."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "he will use all possible means to get news of Tcnemi, and he will communicate them to the general in chief, who will have his headquarters in Calcinato. General Kilmame is warned that the division of General Serurier leaves Ghedi to go to Mezzane, on the Chiese."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will warn his division that the bread to be distributed to the troops will be made up of half wheat and half maize; that this very healthy food cannot be refused by the troops."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier will dispose of his artillery and his troops on horseback, in order "to draw as much benefit as possible from it. As it is to be presumed that he will meet the enemy, that he must attack with vigour and close, he will recommend the greatest order in the march."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As soon as he arrives at Borghetto Bridge, he will notify the Chief of Staff. He will issue the order hereunder to General Beaumont, and he will ensure his execution."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The enemy abandoned us, in his hasty flight, 5 artillery pieces, 9 casings and a large quantity of ammunition, as well as the pharmacy of his ambulances. His entire line is in disarray, and he withdraws with haste by the road to Tyrol, where the Republicans pursue him."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached'the relationship of the Borghetto fight and the passage of the Mincio. I see with satisfaction that Milan is beginning to be quieter."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I arrive in this city, Citizens Directors, to leave tomorrow morning. It is very large and very beautiful. I leave there a good garrison, to stand master of the three bridges that are here on the Adige."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I believe that you must strongly hold for the French to wear it, and that the insult that was made be repaired."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "By means of this Armistice Coin n' 570. 374 CORRESPONDAXCE DE. with Naples, we are able to dictate to Rome all the conditions that we like;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The armistice that we concluded the day before yesterday will, I hope, be the preamble to peace."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Your young cousin came to me yesterday; he seems to me active, albeit still a little young. I will hold him with me; he will soon be able to face the peril and distinguish himself."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I recommend this object to you as one of those who essentially care about the salvation of the army. Brescia and Verona must provide you with resources for this distribution;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I look forward to your reply to the 1,800 homilies that I have asked you to have put in Coni, in order to be able to pull the garrison out of it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "the service is ready to miss every day, by the arbitrariness that is put in each division to retain the means of carts that carry the goods there. The chief authorising officer will make known this order to all the administrations of the army."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The intention of the Chief General is that the Pavie garrison will provide 100 men at the Plaisance Bridge, and that there will be only 100 garrison men at Lodi, at Pizzighettone, 150, at Cremone, 50, at Casai, 50, and at Cassano, 150;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will bring to trial, Citizen General, all the members of the old municipality of Pavia who have been arrested. They will be tried by a military commission that you will appoint for this purpose."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The divisional general Serurier was ordered to take command, not only of the troops forming the blockade of Mantua, but also of the entire Mantuan. He would ensure the disarmament of the communes and maintain a good police force throughout the scope of the command entrusted to him."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We are accustomed here to being freed. Young people come in crowds to ask for service in our bodies; we do not accept it, because (jue it is, I believe, confraternity with the laws;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "H will have at his orders the 6" and 7 battalions of grenadiers and the 12" light infantry half brigade, as well as the 22" regiment of horse hunters."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will pass through your territory, brave Tyroleans, to compel the Vienna Court to a peace necessary for Europe as for its subjects; this is your own cause that I will defend."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You, Citizen General, will give the order to the citizen Aymé, captain of the genius, to go to Alexandria, to command the weapon of the genius in the fortress of Alexandria."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As soon as I knew that the countryside was open at the Rhine, I made walk a column at Lake Corne, which occupied and de-'26."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Everything's fine. I kiss you. The latest news from Paris is from 19. Nothing new. I've had some fifteen robber leaders arrested murdering our soldiers."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We have set up a lot of batteries on the Genoa River; today we would have to sell the cannons and ammunition to the Genoese, in order not to have to keep them, and to be able to find them if necessary."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The assistant to General Warrant Officers Ballet will leave today, at nine o'clock in the evening, with 150 infantry men and 30 dragons, who will be returned at the same time to Alexandria's gate."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The fighters of the 24' regiment who brought them to Pavie will take them to Acqui; in Acqui, a detachment of the garrison will escort them to Cherasco;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "If you think you need a few scout companies, you will instruct General Masséna, who will pass them to you."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "They did not expect that with 800 honors I would have promptly punished Pavia's rebels."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We found in Fort Urban 50 well-stocked cannon pieces, 5,000 caliber rifles and a very good model, and scapegoat ammunition to feed six hundred men for two months."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He has beaten them all, killed them 40 men and taken 50 prisoners. You will find attached copy'of the requisition I made to the government commissioners and the measures they have taken to this end."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We are in Bologna; we seized Fort Urbain, where we found 50 cannon pieces and 5,000 caliber rifles. Be quick to remove this naughty fort from Milan."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I would like you to bring him to His Royal Highness. If you want to talk to me, come here before tomorrow morning."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As a result of article 1" of the armistice that we have concluded ', the intention of the Executive Board."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am now learning that, as a result of a general order given not to let go of what would be going from Bologna to Florence, it could be that Mr Manfredini could not have passed, and that he was still in Bologna."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached, my dear Masséna, a copy of the armistice that I have concluded with the King of the Two Sicilies, and the orders of the King of Naples to the commander of his cavalry in Rrescia, Rergame and Crema."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I gave the order to General Robert to go to Porto-Legnago on the Adige with the 99" half-brigade, today the 51% and two pieces of light artillery."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Hulin battalion leader is ordered to take temporary command of Livorno Square."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will also inquire about the means of obtaining supplies. When this establishment is insured, for both officers and soldiers, what must wax tomorrow in the day, General Vaubois will report to the Chief General."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "An hour before we entered Livorno, an English frigate removed two French buildings worth 500,000 pounds. The governor allowed them to be removed under the fire of his batteries, which is contrary to the intentions of Your Royal Highness and the neutrality of the port of Livorno."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "They took; 15 paintings in Parma, âO in Modena, 25 in Milan, 40 in Bologna, 10 in Ferrara. Total. 110 These scientists also made an abundant harvest in Pavia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The passage of the Rhine is the happiest operation for the army 1 Room n° 676."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I wrote to the minister of the navy to warn him that he could send commissioners to Rome to receive up to four million in cash."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "This was the signal of the attack. The weapons on the arm, and without firing a single blow, our soldiers climbed the steep rocks, killed 100 men, took 200 prisoners, with 400 tents and all the luggage."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The reinforcements arrived at the enemy to 31,000 men, 10,000 Tyroleans, 18,000, rest of the army of Beaulieu, 8,000, garrison of Mantua. Total. 77,000 men. This is the strength of our army • Masséna Division."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached the note which the Secretary of State communicated to the citizen Faypoult, and which he sent to me. You will also find attached a letter from Minister Faypoult concerning the affairs of Genes;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Berihier is furious about the imaginary victory that the German gazetteers are winning at Beaulieii over us. As for me, I find that these gentlemen are right to seek comfort by the only means left to them:"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will send 8 or 10,000 shotguns and five or six thousand powder there in succession. I will have a few brochures printed in the proper style, and from the moment we are well prepared, I think it would be necessary to pass there the citizen Saliceti, the commissioner of the government."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier will have for this operation, regardless of the wing parts of his division, three pieces of 8, and three shells of light artillery, and the 19"" half-brigade of battle infantry."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have no doubt that you would order it as soon as possible; otherwise these villages would be exposed to the just resentment of the army, and I will set a terrible example on them."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna is ordered to send a reconnaissance of 300 infantry men and 300 cavalry men, who will go on the way from Verona to Roveredo through the Pantena Valley."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "For this purpose you will use eight pieces of 12 and two of 33, of those found in Verona. You will care that they are specially supplied with machine guns."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I had sent 600 horses to take convoys to Coni, Vado, to the army dos Alpes; all this died on the way, since since that time I have not heard of it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will also take to Verona the two pieces of 8 which are there and which will replace in Torri the two pieces of 4 which are there. Order the citizens Maubert, commander of the genius, and Carrère, commander of the artillery, to go, in the night, to Verona."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "But I think, at a glance, that 500 men, distributed in these different rooms, will be more than enough to prevent the enemy from approaching, and defend the enclosure. There will be a sufficient guard body on each bridge, with barriers that will be practiced for this purpose."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "the 4% 11% 17% 18' and 22* light half brigades, the 18" and 32" line, and provisionally the 11" line, intended to be part of the division of General Sauret. General Masséna will dispose and order, until further order, the movements of the division of this general;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier is warned that he continues to command the siege of Mantua, having at his orders the 19% 45" and 69° half-battle brigades, and three battalions that will be provided to him by the divisions Masséna and Augereau."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Brigadier-General Ranipon is ordered to immediately leave for Zevio one of the battalions under his command; this battalion will be replaced at the moment by two others which he will ask General Masséna."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna will gather as soon as possible, at his camp in Bussolengo, all the troops he will have available."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The two gentlemen who will bear this letter to you, Citizens Directors, are deputies of the Legion of Ferrara. In that country, as in Bologna, one is very tired of papal power, and one very sincerely desires another order of things."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached. Citizens Directors, the copy of the letter I wrote to the citizen Miot', who kindly took on the task of going to Rome to activate the receipt of our contributions."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Prince of Relmonte-Pignatelli, Citizens Directors, made me the openings on the Emperor as I sent them to you. I asked him officially in writing;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "prevent any kind of communication, under any pretext, and stop all the buildings, none of them having to cross the lake, unless it is around Peschiera and Salo."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General directs you to ensure that the work of the vessel bridge on the Adige is completed as soon as possible;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn him that a squadron of the 5" regiment of dragons is in Brescia to be part of the reserve, and that the orders are also given for the two pieces of light artillery that I announce to him."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Order General Kilmaine to surrender, as soon as possible, h Castelnovo, with 1,000 men and four pieces of light artillery."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will send out, with six caissons of infantry, the shells and the pieces of 12 that are in the park; he will keep only 200 garrison men in Peschiera;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I look forward to receiving information on the division of General Sauret; you have given me nothing but imperfections."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I look forward to Berthier, with the officers of the staff. Circumstances are quite critical. Tomorrow's day will, I hope, be more honourable."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The moments are precious; I entrust the execution of these measures to your wisdom and to your ordinary prudence...."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Masséna will send a body of 1,500 men to occupy the bridge of Valeggio; the rest of his division will be placed behind the Mincio and Peschiera."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Augereau will take a position behind the Molinella in Gasllaro, and since he has only half a brigade, it is essential that you help him. General Masséna will defend the head of the line, from Peschiera to Goito."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will be careful to enlighten his right to recognize the movements that the enemy could make by Goito. The chief general will see him this morning in Montechiaro and will determine with him the work of the cavalry."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Jo warns you that we have had a general affair today, 16; that on the points of altercation the enemy has been completely beaten;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will arrive in Brescia at night. You will also want them to prepare 1,800 rations, which will make a total of 5,800 rations for 5,800 prisoners who arrive in Brescia tonight."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you, General, that the division of General Masséna has withdrawn from Lonato to compete, with the other divisions of the corps of attack, against Wurmscr, between Castiglione and Mantua."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Half of the cavalry is ordered to follow this movement and cover the right flank of General Augereau. General Dommarlin must make available four pieces of light artillery;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Beaumont will send half of his cavalry, with two pieces of light artillery, an General Masséna, who is ordered to go to Peschicra."
sourceTitle: To In The General Beaumont', Brescia, 1796-08-05
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General provisionally entrusts General Fiorella with the command of the division of General Seruricr. Orders are given to complete the bodies that are lacking."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The commander of the axillary will give his orders for the great park to go to the plain, between Castiglione and Lonato."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Brigadier General Guieu, with 600 men of the 15" light infantry half brigade, is contained in a large house in Salo, and there, braves all the efforts of the enemy, who surrounded him from all sides."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "By order of the Chief General. War Deploy. 8M. — TO THE MUNICIPALITY OF CASTIGLIONE. General Quarter, Castiglionc, 19 thermal year IV"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Despinoy will go to Alexandria to take command of the fortress of this square."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The citadel will be occupied by at least one hundred men, as well as all the gates of the city; but its main forces will be placed at those of St.Georges and Vescovo."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Dallemagne is warned that the chief general will be returned tomorrow morning to Brescia, and that his intention is to fan a movement with all his division to attack the enemies at Roccad'Anfo;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General requests you, Mr. Governor, to inform him of the steps you have taken at your request."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Half of his division will be placed in Marmirolo and the other in Borgoforte. He will make his arrangements so that enemy troops can enter the square and intercept communication."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The latter shall communicate to him the instructions he has received on the service of that division."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You would like to send a patrol of fifteen men on horseback, to arrest Abbé Zerbi in Soncino, and have him translated into prisons in Milan."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will inform him that I have given orders that it be supplied for 1,500 men for ten days, and that there are always a hundred gunners to put the artillery of this place into service."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "he will give the 538 h'. command of his division to General Garnier with the necessary instructions."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have just ordered that three hundred of them be put in each convent. Please take steps to ensure that they are treated and treated as they should be;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have just sent to the door of the six convents a guard, and I give the order CORRESPOXDANCK DE NAPOLÉOM I." — A.V IV (179fij. 539) to the director of hospitals to send there three hundred sick per convent."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general will send the 3* battalion of the 85" half-brigade, which is here and which will be used to cover Brescia, to Sabbio tomorrow morning. A body of 100 horses has been carried today to Collio;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached several copies of the relationship'that you want."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received the letter that Your Royal Highness honoured me on July 13th. It did not arrive to me until very late, which, together with the many events that have just occurred, has put some delay in my response."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I learn, gentlemen, that the former Jesuits, the priests and the religious disturb public tranquility."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you. General, that the general in chief, believing you were ill in Milan, had provisionally entrusted the command of the troops on horseback of the army to divisional general Dubois."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Moreover, I learn that the company Flacbat must take them for 400,000 pounds:"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general is in charge of me. General, to congratulate you on the integrity of your victories. They make our position in Rrescia out of sight of some kind of worry;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you, Citizen Orderer, that the division of General Saurct is in Lodrone, with about 5,000 men. It is of the last importance that it be fed by Brescia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General has received, General, the letter by which you inform him of the results of your movements and of the position in which you are in."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will be attached to his division twelve pieces of light artillery and six of 5 or 4. Same order to General Masséna; he will give his orders and himself will ensure that the deck of ships ordered on the Adige is completed as quickly as possible."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We need a large amount of biscuit, mainly in Verona, Brescia and Peschiera, and finally a lot of means of transport. Gather all our means and let me know what we can count on for all these objects of the first necessity."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Mandate me what are the battalions that make up the 6 half-brigade that you announce, of what is composed 10% the moment it will start, and finally the state of all the other bodies that are announced to us."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "he will consult with the artillery commander to select and have provided the most proper rifles for this service. He will arrange for 100 dragons of the 5th regiment, at least, to be armed with rifles in the current of the decade."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received the note you have written to me, where you wish to be instructed about the movements of French troops in the territory of His Royal Highness. I have the honour to inform you. Sir, that the Minister of France in Florence will notify His Royal Highness about these various objects."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Murat will lead with him, at Casal-Maggiore, the 51" half-brigade, his two artillery pieces and the detachment of the 21" regiment of hunters he must have."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you, General, that according to the provisions of the Chief General, you must immediately go to Storo, headquarters of the division of General Sauret, which you will raise in his command. You will have under your command Brigadier Generals Guieu, Menard and Dallemagne."
sourceTitle: To In General L Alibois, Brescia, 1796-08-21
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Since the majority of you are well-intentioned, force these few stubborn men to submit; their foolish conduct tends to attract the fury of war upon their homeland."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The authorising commissioner is also required to have 60,000 biscuit rations, 120,000 live water rations, 60,000 flour rations and oats boarded on the Adige for -4,000 horses for ten days;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "If you want, Citizens Directors, to go to Xaples, seriously consider sending me reinforcements. If you could hold what you're announcing from the Rbin's army, that would be enough for me."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He will have Austrian rifles collected by soldiers who are in front of his forehead and will make a pile of them. General Lespinasse will have them loaded on the cars that bring sustenance, and that will remain at the disposal of this general."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "We are walking on this point tomorrow; but it is to be assumed that the enemy, seeing that it could be cut by Padua, is on Porto-Legnago."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Kilmaine will leave with the garrison of Verona, infantry and cavalry, to go to Isola-della-Scala."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 2'" will leave on 2(3, to arrive on the 1" additional day; The '.V will leave on the 27th, to arrive on the 2'' additional day;"
sourceTitle: To General Warrant Officer Pascalîs, Montebello, 1796-09-10
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will cause all the prisoners to leave, by evacuating them by 500, and the general in chief authorizes you to use temporarily the bourgeois guard of Milan for the escort of the said prisoners;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "His intention is also that you will evacuate all the forces that are in Borgoforte on Marcaria. You will hold all the troops you have at your orders ready to attack tomorrow, according to the order you will receive."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "When this operation is complete, he will leave Bassano, with the 11" half-brigade, to go without delay to Verona, where he and this half-brigade will receive new orders."
sourceTitle: To General Of Luugade Bourxet, Verona, 1796-09-17
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 2* battalion of the 75" half-brigade, currently in Livorno, will leave at the receipt of the present to go to Ferrara, where he will occupy the citadel until further order."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As soon as he has gathered about 1,500 men, he will send them to raise the 18* half-brigade do battle, which will come to Rovcrbella. General Masséna will go to Porto-Lcgnago to take a review of the 4" half-brigade of light infantry."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 8* battalion of grenadiers will go to Roverbella, where he will remain until further order, with the 18* half-brigade of battle. General Masséua will appoint a general officer to command the troops of his division who will temporarily remain in Roverbella."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "This battalion is to be used to work at the fortifications of Pizzighettone, Peschiera and Porto-Legnago. The men will be captured in the various provinces of Lombardy;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The same order to the commander of the Place de Bologna, to consult with the Senate, and to organize throughout Bolonais a battalion of pioneers, composed of five companies of 120 men each."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached an order of 25,000 pounds to cover the expenses you deny. You will transport yourself to Ostiglia;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I had already issued a mandate of 20,000 pounds to the citizen Faultrier. Please do not forget to place two coins in Ostiglia."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order the 5* and 9" dragon regiments to proceed to Brescia. The six half-brigades above named must have their brigade chiefs and battalion chiefs present in the bodies."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order that the priest Zerbi, of Soncino, arrested by my orders, be released."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Eunemi is still far from your walls, but it enters into the combinations of war that you are besieged from one moment to another;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order General Willot to requisition detachments of the National Guard, taken from among the citizens most attached to the Republic and most interested in the maintenance of law and order."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I would like the localities to allow the rapid construction of a enclosure around Borgoforte, to put 1,500 men in a shelter; I think it would be possible to use its waters favorably."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will flood it at Dolce; you will see how well the right hand of a ii<的ne who, from this square on the banks of Tadige, would go to Moute-Baldo, and from there to Lake Garda."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Help us as quickly as possible, if you want us to continue sending you 700,000 francs. Estimate, consideration and attachment. BOXAPARTE. P. S. I ask you above all to pass us rifles as soon as possible;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I ask you to order that all wounded persons in service be transferred to Lyon, where."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The contribution that was to be fully paid, for the last term, the 4 Messidor, is not yet paid."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The name Rey, second lieutenant in the 51* half-brigade, allowed himself to strip an Austrian officer, who had been taken prisoner of war in the last case of Governmentolo."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have the honour to communicate to Your Holiness a manifesto which circulates in the Roman, in order to know whether it is official or if it is published by the enemies of religion and Your Holiness."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will have the Commissioner of the Flach' Wars arrested and taken to Milan, wherever he is."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached, Citizens Directors, a proclamation 'on Modena. These little regents warn to conspire, I warned them."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "One would stop there: 1° the organization of the Italian legion; 2° one would make a kind of federation, for the common defence."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is not my intention that the artillery workshops should be busy repairing the guns of the lumbar lion, having already a large number of rifles of the army to be repaired; the State Congress should be responsible for repairing their rifles."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is that: 1° we have lived for a long time of requisitions; 2° we have had food in nature from Modena, Parma, Ferrara and Bologna; 3° the Republic of Venice has supplied us and still provides us with a lot of food;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "1 "They have received fourteen million; they have paid only six, and they refuse to discharge the mandates given by the treasury, at less than fifteen or twenty percent."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached a letter'which you will bring to the congregation, and you will take steps with it for the prompt lifting of this legion. Everything must be done in the name of the congress and it must be completed as soon as possible."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will pass two pieces of 3 or 5, supplied, in Lodi, for the defense of the bridge; two pieces of the same calibre in Cassano, to defend also the bridge, and four pieces of 3 at Trezzo Castle, on the Adda."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is, I believe, in the spirit of war, in the interests of both armies, to have access to an arrangement. Return to the Emperor your person, or even cavalry and infancy;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "But, having found 64,000 in Livorno, belonging to the king of Spain, I made take 20,000, which I had brought to the army."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I thought the Lombards were the most patriotic people in Fltalia, but I'm beginning to believe that Bologna, Ferrara, Reggio, Modena outperform them in energy;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
