displayText: "The provisional 12'' will leave the day after tomorrow with two cannon pieces of 3. The provisional 55" half-brigade will send, from tomorrow, a battalion to Fort Urbain, another one to Bologna;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You shall cause the seal to be placed on his papers, and you shall send him away under safe escort; you shall also send me all his papers."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "For this purpose, each brigade general, assisted by a war commissioner, will review every ten days, the 8, IH and 28 of each month, the bodies he will have at his command;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The French Government still allows me to reopen peace negotiations; everything can still be arranged. The grieving, so cruel for the peoples, has terrible results for the defeated:"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Modena, Reggio, Ferrara and Rologne, gathered in congresses, stopped a raise of 2,800 men, under the title of 1" Italian legion. The enthusiasm is very great; the peasants who carried food in Mantua came to teach us themselves the hidden roads they held."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Only six pieces of light artillery will remain in the army by each of the divisions of General Masséna and General Augcareau, 1 Exhibit 11° 1101."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "First agent of the Republic in Lombardy, it is to you to destroy all abuses, and to restore things as they should be. The State Congregation is necessarily responsible for supervising CORRESPOXDAACE DE XAPOLEOIV I"."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 52'=half brigade will be directed to Tortone, where it will receive new orders. All other troops, either detachments, depots or artillery, will also be directed to this place, where they will receive new orders."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Sir, matters of the utmost importance making me wish to have a conference with you, I beg you to want to take you to Peschiera, at two o'clock after noon, where I will be given back. I beg you to believe in the feelings of consideration and esteem, etc."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached a paragraph that I am currently receiving from the Executive Board. Please, therefore, from comCORRESPOXD.WCE DE XAPOLÉOX I'."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief authorising officer is required to have the Verona citadel, for 20 days and for 600 men, and Fort Saint-Pierre, also for 20 days and for 100 men, immediately supplied. He will give notice of when these two places will be supplied."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You know that the 75'' half-brigade, with 3,000 men, has orders to be tomorrow in Montebello. The intention of the chief general is to rest there at least two days;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will report to me on the steps you have taken in this regard. You will notify the officers that you will leave that they must indicate where they will have withdrawn."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general ordered General Lespinasse to transfer as quickly as possible to Vicence 100,000 cartridges, of which 50,000 for the 75 half-brigade, which was absolutely lacking, and the remainder to the division of General Masséna, in replacement of those she might have consumed."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The intention of the Chief General is that, as soon as the movements 1 On the night of the 13th year 14."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Guillaume, commander at Peschicra, is ordered to immediately leave a detachment of 92 men from the 5P half-brigade, who will join their half-brigade through Verona;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "By way of Montehello, this officer will appear at the General Staff. It is recommended that he bring the greatest accuracy in the execution of this order."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Citizen, from the establishment of a road that leads from the boat bridge on the Adige to Incanale: this measure is absolutely necessary and requires all your activity."
sourceTitle: To Commander Of The Genius, Verona, 1796-11-05
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 2nd battalion, which arrives the day after tomorrow in Peschiera, will follow the movement of the first. The 4* light infantry half brigade will remain in Verona, or will go to Rivoli, as agreed with General Kilmaine."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Austrians have suffered a lot, and I hope that we will beat them completely at the first meeting."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Lcspinasse will pass, as soon as possible, balls that are said to have arrived today in Porto-Legnago. He will evacuate behind the Adda all the useless pieces that are on this side, on any point."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "On the representation made to the Chief General that the artillery lacks carters, General Lespinasse is authorized to accept and use for this service the soldiers of goodwill who will present themselves;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "During the night of the 24th to 25th, I threw a boat bridge at Ronco, where we passed this river. I was hoping to arrive in the morning at Villanova, and by this way to remove the enemy's artillery parks, his luggage, and attack the enemy army by the flank and its backs."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "This young man had become familiar with the weapons, he walked several times at the head of the columns;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Muiron died by my side, on the battlefield of Arcole. You lost a husband who was dear to you, I lost a friend to whom I had long been attached;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "If not, I ask you to order the citizen Haller, who did not come in 1 In Exhibits Nos 1288, 1289, 1439 and 1490, the general"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte

archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Chief General sees with the greatest discontent that, despite his order of the 8 Germinal, women continue to follow the army; he sees that it is above all the officers who prolong this abuse by following their own and thus setting an example for the soldiers."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Guieu will also order General Bon to leave at Mauterndorf 30 infantry men, who, with 30 horses, will occupy the fork of the roads of Saint-Michel, Murau and Radstadt."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "But, if it is to be a journey to peace so desired and so useful to the two peoples, I consent without difficulty to your desires. The French Republic has often manifested to His Majesty its desire to put an end to this cruel struggle."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I pass a few gunners there, and I send a battalion of the half-brigade 19® to Livorno."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will see that that of General Delmas must be composed of the 12* and:26'' light infantry half brigades, the 39" and 93* battle, and six cannon pieces;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Italians, accustomed to not being interested in the show and playing in their lodges, would not, I believe, frequent your theatre."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is necessary to seek. Citizen, to reconcile, as far as possible, the esteem and attachment of the people of Klagenfuçt and the countryside. Therefore, you must strive to suppress, as much as possible, the abuse of the exaggerated demands that so cruelly weigh upon this people."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General directs Warrant Officer General Solignac to reimburse immediately the 1,000 ducats of contribution he has collected at Leoben; he will pass the receipt that the Chief General requires within 24 hours."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "From what you write to me, Citizen Minister, on the account of Mr. Spinola d'Arquata, I wish like you that he could enter into the usual state;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1.""There will be friendship and good intelligence between His Majesty the Emperor and King and the French Republic; hostilities between the two powers will cease from today."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached, Citizens Directors, a note that has just given me the plenipotentiaries of the Emperor, containing the assurance of ratification."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general ordered General Bernadotte to leave Gratz, with his entire division, tomorrow 6, to go to Laybach."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Yesterday 4, the chief general reviewed the division commanded by General Serurier; he made known to the army order his satisfaction at the attention and precision of the soldiers in carrying out the manoeuvres;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The citizen Laugier came out of Trieste; he was met by the fleet of the Emperor, composed of 8 to 10 gunboats; he fought part of the day with them, after which he sought refuge under the cannon of Venice."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have read only with indignation, gentlemen, the letter that you wrote to me concerning the murder of Laugier."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General is instructing me to ask you, gentlemen, that he give orders that there be no hostility against the Republic of Venice for four days, starting tomorrow."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier is ordered to continue his road on the 20th to reach Sacile. His command will extend from the Piave to the Tagliamento, that is, the Conegliano and the part of Friuli on the right bank of the Tagliamento."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: ""The next 24 Thermidor, he was of name water judged and acquitted by the council" permanent war."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The loan of 40,000 francs that you have provided in times of shortage praises your zeal; it is right that you should be reimbursed for it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "However, I would be very pleased if he left one of us in Venice. I hope that, for the promptness you will put in this matter, the whole expedition will be gone no later than three days after receiving this order."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I give the order to hold 1,000 men in Ancona ready to be taken on board, so that, if circumstances so required, you can quickly receive reinforcements."
sourceTitle: To Citizen Of The Republic, Mombello, 1797-05-26
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I also urge you to gather all your efforts and to send to the said islands, regardless of the troops you already have there, 7 or 800 men with some armed buildings."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Serenissimo Doge, I received the letter that Your Serenity bothered to write to me. I delayed answering it until I received the information about what had happened in Genoa and of which Your Serenity gave me the first news."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Lombard legion and as a result of an order they claim to have of me, travel the towns and villages from Pieve to Ceva, and commit disorder there. I beg you to consult with Mr."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "According to the explanations you have given me, Citizen General, I approve the departure of two vessels of 64 for the expedition of Corfu;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Your Serenity will find below the note of the persons whom, in accordance with the convention we have made, I thought it appropriate to choose as the ones most suitable to form the provisional government."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will seize all the circumstances to do something that 1 This order has not been found."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I thought I had informed you that I had granted the city of Verona the silverware of the churches to be part of its contribution. If the letters of exchange sent to you by the municipality of Verona are not accepted, write to your agent so that he would warn it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Serurier will give you twenty-two flags that still remain of those that the army took in the last events of the campaign."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have the honour to transmit to you herewith a memorandum presented to General Bonaparte in favour of the name Louis Imperatori, a Piedmontese merchant, now in Algiers."
sourceTitle: To French Consul A Alger, Milan, 1797-06-13
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I hardly learn, Citizens, that there are troubles in the city of Bologna;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As a result, you would like to order: Article 1. — The Brcscian will extend to the Mincio."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Citizens, I learn with the greatest displeasure that, in a moment of baldness, the statue of André Doria was overturned."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is expressly forbidden to suffer from the property of that citizen. The civil authorities and military authorities remain responsible for providing relief and assistance in case of need."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The effect of this gathering was to destroy three or four French soldiers who believed they were serving their homeland by walking under the orders of the citizen Hibert;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Requests for leave to leave the body temporarily, either for service or for personal affairs, shall be addressed by the boards of directors, with reasons, to the Brigadier General;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received, General Citizen, your letter of the 25th Prairial, with the state of the contributions that the Bavarian voter and the Swabian circle owe. We will make the best use of it as possible."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I flatter myself that soon it will resume the same chandelier that it had in the past. The army of Italy, which has contributed in something to give consideration to the French Republic in Italy, is by this very fact to have rendered the city of Marseille a special service."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Citizens Directors, you will find attached the peace treaty concluded with the Republic of Venice. I have the honour to warn you that, during the conclusion of this treaty in Milan, the revolution was made in Venice and the Grand Council had already removed its powers."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Government would therefore like you to give him Tordre to leave Paris. Mr. Spinola was also recalled; however, among the Patriotic Genoese, he enjoys some consideration;"
sourceTitle: To Minister For External Relations, Milan, 1797-07-12
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As I see that things are always at the same point, I will wait, to go to Udine, for the arrival of the long-awaited Mr. Baptiste. I have sent you, through a mail, the latest news of Paris;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "11 There is not one man here who likes to perish weapons by hand better than being murdered in a cul-de-sac in Paris. As for me, I am accustomed to a total abdication of my interests;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It is difficult, I believe, to question today that the Emperor wants to save time. What is the reason? It is difficult to imagine it, unless to see it in the royalist newspapers, the club of Clicliy and the return of the emigrants."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received the letter Your Royal Highness has kindly written to me on 14 July. I will always do what I can to be pleasant to him and to contribute to his peace and happiness."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The commander of Lombardy must act in Lombardy and Milan as if there were only 2 or 300 men in Milan to keep the citadel; for it is possible that from one moment to the next he is actually reduced to the only Lombard troops to keep the citadel:"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached a copy of the letter written to me by General Clarke. Mr. Rapfisle left Mombello on the 5 Messidor;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am now receiving your letter from 28. I hope to receive one tomorrow with the account of the interview you have had with Mr."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "attached'to the Executive Board of the Cisalpine Republic and send it to all divisions of the army."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have passed the 58th half-brigade, which is 2,500 men, to the division of General Victor, and, at the slightest movement, I will make you pass the cavalry division of General Dugua. Make sure that your artillery is well supplied and able to enter the countryside."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I do not see any inconvenience, sir, that you will pass on the line of demarcation the troops which you will judge appropriate to maintain good order and tranquillity in the States of His Majesty."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I therefore believe it is necessary for you to send here 3,000 cavalry men, among whom I would like at least 1,500 large cavalry. I would also like three new artillery companies on horseback."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am of the opinion to simply reply to the note of the Emperor's plenipotentiaries that the agreement signed at Leoben, the 5 Prairial, provided for everything; that we relate entirely to its content;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "After all this will be done, ask the bishop of Vicence to send missionaries to that country to preach to them peace, obedience, under penalty of hell. To this end, bring to 1 Presumed Date, 8 thermal year V"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Already almost four months have passed since that time; there are three that the undersigned have made known to the plenipotentiaries of S."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The first time that some of Your Lordship's parents will have an opportunity to come to Italy, I beg her to kindly address them to me; I will have a real pleasure in giving them marks of the esteem I have for your person and your compatriots."
sourceTitle: To Head Of The Maxiotes, Milan, 1797-07-30
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will order General Bon to go to Crémone to take command of the 1rd half brigade and follow the movements. You will order Warrant Officer General Gilly young to go to headquarters in Milan to receive new orders."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you that I order General Baraguey-d'Hilliers to distribute the 5,000 rifles he has in Venice, namely: 2,000 in Palmanova; You will order General Guillaume not to distribute them to anyone without my express order, and to keep them always in good condition;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It will force the enemy to put another 5,000 or 6,000 men in Oalmatia. The Austrians occupied Ragusa and the mouths of the Cattaro;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Sir, by one of your friends, learn that you are deprived of the pension that you enjoyed in Venice. The French Republic makes a special case of the great talents that distinguish you."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "From now on, Citizen General, that I will have news of the arrival of Mr."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General orders: Article 1. — The cisalpine Republic shall pay to the fund of 230 er. Year one million a month, all parts of the territory of the cisalpine Republic shall be exempt from requisition in any form whatsoever."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Seem to be the company of the guides on foot, tomorrow morning, at the time and place you will consider most suitable;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have the honour to warn you that, since this officer is essential to the army, I would only have him in Genes for a certain time."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "But you alone must reserve the right to grant this permission, so that it will never become very important. As for the towns or cities you will consider necessary to grant some weapons for their police, I do not see any inconvenience either."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I order Venice to the authorising officer of the Navy Roubaud and to General Baraguey-d'Hilliers to make speak of Venice two good gunboats each carrying a bronze coin of 24."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — In accordance with the arrangements made with the municipality of Venice, a store of all the materials, ammunition and rigging necessary for the three ships and two frigates that are under construction shall be set up."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I leave tomorrow, Citizen General, to go to the countryside, near Codroipo. If the intention of the plenipotentiaries is to stay in the countryside, I will tell General Victor to give himself the necessary cares to find suitable accommodation in the surroundings."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You have under your command the 12th light infantry half brigade with two squadrons of the 8th dragons for the garrison of Milan. You have the mobile column that is in Monza, with 4,000 men."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I ask you to take an interest in him with the Government of Genoese, and to facilitate him in any way to be employed in any part."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He gives us 10,000 men; that's a lot. We will also make one with the Genoese, who will provide us 4,000 men. All this is very good against the peasants and the mass liftings that the Emperor garlic."
sourceTitle: To Minister For External Relations, Milan, 1797-08-22
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will also pass 15,000 francs to the payer of Palmanova, to make them available to the engineer officer for the fortifications of this place. You will bear this sum in account to the general commanding the genius of the army, who will settle with you at the first opportunity."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have the honour to convey to you the letter I am writing to the Minister of Finance;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I think we should have an army of 12,000 cavalrymen and 80,000 infantry men on the Rhine; have a body making the siege of Manheim and masking the four strongholds of the Rhine;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "In concluding the Treaty, we shall have regard to the wise observation" which is contained. We have exchanged our full powers. We have spent two sittings drafting the second minutes."
sourceTitle: To Minister For External Relations, Passariano, 1797-09-03
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — The army is warned that it will start the next 2 salesman."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will also order the citizen Giovanni, commander of the place of Mantua, to go also to Genes, to perform the duties of General Warrant Officer and to work for the organization of the Genoese battalions. He will continue to count in his corps"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It seems to me very impractical. However, please see Admiral Brueys and General Sugny, and consult with them on what they could do, if that happened."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will also want to take on the first made clothes for the frame 100 complete clothing, and pass them immediately to Peschiera."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — The German citizen, captain of the frigate, will immediately travel to Peschiera, to take over the command of the navy of Lake Garda."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: ", I have read, Citizen, the Relationship of the Genus Revolution that you sent me. I know few works as simple, as true and as persuasive."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please, Citizen Minister, take on my account five hundred copies of the Relation of the Revolution of Genes made by Pussielgue;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — The first salesman is the anniversary of the foundation of the Republic."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — The supply of a seat which exists at that time in the castle of Soncino will be transported to Mantouc. General Mioliis will be careful that it is not distracted from the supply."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief General shall adopt the following: Article I." — Provisionally, any export by sea of grains of all kinds shall be prohibited."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive in the moment, Citizen, your pastoral care of September 5th. I thought I heard one of the twelve apostles. This is how St Paul spoke. How respectable religion is when it has ministers like you!"
sourceTitle: To Citizen Archbishop Of Embarrassments, Passariano, 1797-09-10
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I agree with you that the conduct of the Government has been weak. In difficult circumstances, resources can only be found in courage and firmness."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "line troop, and, if necessary, let the enemies of freedom know that I have 100,000 men to join your large national guard and erase up to the traces of the enemies of your freedom."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will find attached, Citizen General, two decrees of the Executive Board, of the 4 and 1 Fructidor, which I only receive at this moment."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

displayText: "I have instructed the brigade chief of the 7th Hussards to send you 3 (5 saddles and 36 flanges, who will leave tomorrow. The members of the couch will be settled on the taxes of the country."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please let me know, Citizen General, the sums you need for the various services. Genius and artillery must address the generals commanding their weapon, who will make them pass the money they will need."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Rosette provided 100,000 without difficulty, and Alexandria 300,000. Send to the staff the state of the men you had left in Mansourah;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, chief general, orders: Article 1. — All the horses, mules and camels of the artillery shall be marked with an A."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "My intention is, Citizen, that each house marshal, brigadier and horse guide, be armed with a rifle and a pair of pistols. Each pistol will be bound by a cord, so that it can quickly pull the rifle and the two pistols."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "My intention, Citizen, is to have, for each company of guides, six axes, two excavators, two picks. See to make these tools of a size strong enough to cut trees, fill a ditch or unravel a wall, and however light enough not to bother the rider."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The equipment will consist of Two pieces of 3, Two pieces of 8, Two shells, A field forge, An extension loaded with tools and spare objects. I gave orders to obtain the mules or mules necessary for this artillery division."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Can you replace it? If you can't give them one of 8, give them a howitzer, or a piece of 5 or 3. They have all the necessary horses. For eight days the wheels of the guide box have been sent to the park, and they are not yet repaired."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received very few letters from you; I believe that the one of the 12 Messidor is the second. I hardly learn that there is agitation in the garrison of Malle."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You, Citizen, will go to the commander of the square; you will find there the treasure" Koraim, of Alexandria."
sourceTitle: To Citizens Of The Community, Cairo, 1798-08-28
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will have this house and other properties of the said Code seized, which is with Ibrahim-Boy."
sourceTitle: To Citizen Of The Country, Cairo, 1798-08-28
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Let me know exactly all the news you'd have from General Desaix."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Reorganize this canton. Please buy me for my guides 20 beautiful horses, not included in the number of 150. I do not want to put more than G to 7 louis one."
sourceTitle: To In The General Murat, Cairo, 1798-08-29
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The chief general orders: 1° The contracts awarded to Alexandria for the sale of rice are broken."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Alexandria, Rosette, Damiette and all the main cities are in the same case. Wouldn't there be a way to impose a tax on houses in all the main cities of Egypt to pay for all the police costs?"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I send you, Citizen General, a large number of packages for different consuls. I have put in prints, in order to get there to give news."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Let him know that I hope that he will repair, by good conduct and by the services that he will render us, the bad conduct that he held first. Bonaparte... 31 "S. — AT THE DIVAN" OF THE CAIRE. Headquarters, Cairo, 12 Fructidor an VI"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The government has passed 400,000 pounds to Ancona, 500,000 pounds to Corfu and 600,000 pounds to Malta. I am sending 45,000 pounds today for your service, which, together with the 100,000 I have sent you, form a sum that will put you at your level of need."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: ", Bonaparte, chief general, orders: Article 1. — The exclusive privilege of selling wine and wine from the victim to Alexandria remains removed;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive your letter from 5 Fructidor, from Rosette, Citizen General. I always recommend that you put some cannon pieces to defend the mouth of the Nile."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen General, your letter of the 8 Fructidor, with the letter you sent me from Rear Admiral Ganteaume. I always count on your activity and your zeal."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please, Citizen, let me know the shops of wood, iron, ropes, houses, etc., which were found in Damiette. Damiette is one of the points of Egypt that has the most resources;"
sourceTitle: To Citizen Of The Country, Cairo, 1798-08-30
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "As long as there are 25,000 cartridges in the park, I'll send them to you. I'm assured that Bouch is a bigger place than BenySoueyf;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen General, your letter with the information you give me about the movements of part of the Mameluks on Syria."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I therefore want you to remain convinced of the desire where I am to live in good intelligence with you and to give you all the signs of the most perfect friendship. Bonaparte.. 320C). —Al PACHA OF THE GRAND SEIGNOR IN EGYPT. Headquarters, Cairo, \i Fructidor an VI"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: ", where he ran alone to help several of his comrades without weapons and attacked by the Bedouins."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The flood must not prevent you, Citizen General, from getting the horses that your province must provide. As you have climbed a few riders, send them to Boulàq;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive your letters of 11 and 12. I make myself realize why the six pieces did not arrive in Damiette. ". It is essential that you raise the contribution of 150,000 francs, entirely and without exempting anyone from it;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You can, General Citizen, send different detachments to submit the different villages of the province."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen General, both your letters of 0, 11, and 12 Fructidor. I am not surprised at what happened to the Toriule."
sourceTitle: To In The Genital Kleber, Cairo, 1798-09-04
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen, your letter of the 13 Fructidor and the states attached to it. How is it possible that, for two months since you were an authorising officer in Alexandria, you have not landed the artillery that was in the hold of the Dubois and Causse?"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Caffarelli has sent money to your engineer officer; General Menou has just sent money: so the works of the canal must go vigorously and without any kind of delay."
sourceTitle: To Chief Warrant Officer Brires, Cairo, 1798-09-04
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I had ordered that 20,000 rations be sent three days ago with a convoy of cartridges; the cartridges have arrived and the biscuit is not yet;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, chief general, orders: He will be established in the vicinity of Cairo, near the Nile and in the most pleasant room that can be found, a convalescence hospital. The sick, after leaving the hospital, will spend five or six days in this hospital to recover completely."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, chief general, orders: 1° The 10 Vendemiary will be held a general assembly of all the notables of the fourteen provinces of Egypt. 2° A deputation will consist of three men of law, three traders, three fellahs, sheiks-el-beled and chiefs of Arabs."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You must have received, General Citizen, the shoes and the 200 quintals of flour. We will do research to find the papers that concern the property of the Mameluks of Belbeys province."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Republic, even having served them as spy, will be shot in the day of tomorrow. All its property, furniture and buildings, will be confiscated for the benefit of the Republic."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, general in Cbef, orders: Article 1. — When Alexandria's headquarters store is supplied with 15,000 quintals of rice it must have; That the daily store in Alexandria's Square will have the necessary quantity to feed the garrison for two months;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Have you sent him any since then? 11 Writes me, on the 18th of Fructidor, that the lack of cartridges prevents him from carrying out my orders. Please send him some in the day 50,000."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You spoke to me in your last letter about the Arabs found who had attacked Mansourah; you tell me, in this letter, that they are surrounded by water."
sourceTitle: To At The Gexebal Murat, Cairo, 1798-09-06
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, chief general, orders: Article 1. — Sabbato Adda and Telebi di Figura are appointed high priests of the Jewish nation."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have learned with difficulty that, as a result of your injury, you would remain crippled with an arm. You must comfort yourself with this accident, since you have had it by doing your duty gloriously."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "In fact, I believe that the person who rendered this ship is extremely guilty, since it is found, in his minutes, that he has done nothing to fail it and to put it out of order to be brought."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte. Conini. by M"10 de la Morinière. 3367, — AT THE CITIZEN REGXAL'D DE SAIXT-JEAX-D'AXGELY 2. Headquarters, Cairo, 24 Fructidor an VI"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, general in Cbef, orders: Article 1. — A commercial court will be established in the squares of Cairo, Alexandria, Rosette and Damiette."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The contribution of £00,000, Citizen General, which you have raised on the dealers of Alexandria, will be sold in houses, 1 Room n° 3210."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "This is the cry of all those who come to Cairo, and negligence on this essential point excites complaints. Bonaparte... 3274. _ AL CITIZEN THE ROY, in Alexandria. Headquarters, Cairo, 26 Fructidor an VI"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "of wheat that it will be possible for you, and to have to fire in return tools, cartridges and cannons."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You have done very well, Citizen General, to have a collision hold made at Rosette. The establishment of the four ovens seems sufficient for the moment."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "When I arrived in Egypt at the head of the French army, I made a proclamation in Arabic, on the last day of Moharem, the year 1213 of Hegira, which sees the reasons for my coming."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please have it printed and sent me 600 copies, and send 400 copies to spread in the Archipelago. Please be careful that the names of the signatories are placed right below."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "In your letter of the 23rd, you do not yet tell me that you have received horses. However, you have had to see, by order of the day, that your province had to provide 200 of them."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please, General Citizen, send 50,000 cartridges for Mansourah, to be at the disposal of General Dugua, and 100,000 for Mebailet-el-Kebyr, at the disposal of General Fugière."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Chief Authorising Officer will pass 100,000 rations of biscuit for the said armament to Alexandria."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "According to what Say told us yesterday, Cairo's handling should be at that of the year of Italy in the report from 13 to 18, when we paid 2 sous to the company Julliot;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I beg you, Citizen, to pass on to me the note of all the young men of the polytechnic school who came to the expedition. You will make known to me all those who wish to enter the artillery or the genius."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 30 Fructidor, the payer of the army, in the presence of the financial administrator, will auction all diamonds, gold coins, precious fabrics, etc., which are at his disposal. The minimum will be one third in addition to the estimate made in Cairo."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Let me know, Citizen General, the way you would travel from Mansourah to Belbeys, and from Mansourah to Salheyeh; how you would get there, and how you would pass through your artillery and cavalry."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You will give the order to the citizen Beau Neighbor to go to Belbeys, to take command of the square."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "My intention is that there "is no kind of taxation on wine in Alexandria, nor in any other part of Egypt."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Bonaparte, chief general, orders: Article 1. — A registration office shall be established in each capital city of Egypt, where all titles of property and acts likely to be brought to justice shall be authentic."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "There is, 1 These words, added by the minute, are by the hand of the general"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You may, Citizen, establish as quickly as possible a flying bridge to be used as a communication between the Old Caire and Gyzeh. This flying bridge must be capable of carrying 100 infantry bums and 25 cavalry."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Sheik Sàdàt had received 25,000 paras of the Mint, in anticipation of what was due to him, the first of Moharrem: my intention is that it is not sought on those 25,000 paras;"
sourceTitle: To Citizen Of The Country, Cairo, 1798-09-17
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Tomorrow, at four o'clock after noon, 200 gunners and a detachment of 10 men, composed of workers, carters and pontoons, will pass from Gyzeh to Cairo, in order to be able to attend the festival of the"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I would desire, Citizen General, that you should have given the two pieces of 8 to the guides in the daytime, with the harnesses that you have at your disposal; that in the day of tomorrow, or at the latest the day after tomorrow, you should have given them the two pieces of 3."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "If it were impossible for the park to make such a complete one for the 2 salesman, we could, for that one, remove the knee pads and do anything that could shorten the work. Let me know what this bridge will weigh."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen General, the report, which you send to me, from General Verdier on the outcome of the expedition on the village of Sonbàt. It is with real pleasure that I gave the order to have the citizen Laugier recognized as adjutant general:"
sourceTitle: To In The Général Dugua, Cairo, 1798-09-20
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Let me know if your health puts you in the case of taking command of the province of Beny-Soueyf. After tomorrow leave by the Turkish J that I intend to take command of Atfyeh, with a company of 60 men."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He had to leave yesterday in the evening 50,000 cartridges for your division, with four pieces of 5 and two pieces of 32 for the armament of Damiette. You will take command of the province of Damiette, keeping that of the province of Mansourah."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He missed his fortune. Mourad-Bey, beaten, discouraged, is in a very bad position and ready to sink into the desert. I hope that, by the first mail, I will finally learn the arrival of the Nile in Alexandria and the departure of the objects that we have so long to have for Cairo."
sourceTitle: To Warrant Officer General Bribes, Cairo, 1798-09-21
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The Copts, 1,000; the wife of Mourad-Bey, 8,000; the women of Mameluks, 20,400. All this does not pay. It is very essential however that they hurry, because our needs become urgent"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "A large part drowned; their camels, more than G, 000 sheep were taken. Another part of these robbers was attacked, near Myt-Ghamar, by General Murat, who killed them 40 men, took part of their cattle, and forced them to evacuate the country."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please. General, to activate as much as possible the horse's return to your province, and to send them, as you receive them, to Roulàq. Your province was to provide 50 horses;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I warn you. Citizen, that anyone who wants to see the Pyramids will go to bed tonight in Gyzeh, from here. We will leave tomorrow 3, at six o'clock in the morning."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "13,945 remain, of which 3,945 will be paid in the day of tomorrow, and the remaining 10,000, 1,000 per day."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Most of all, the village of Myt-el-Khaouly must provide you with at least 100 weapons and cannon pieces. They hid them, but I'm sure they have them."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Make known to the aga that I am very-satisfied of the words that one holds in the city against Christians. There must be at this moment hostages of Alenouf at the citadel."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am sending you attached. Citizen, copy of an order of the Chief General concerning the assembly of notables, and the execution which you will be willing to take care of as far as you are concerned. The Chief General wishes that coffee be provided to the members of this assembly."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Articlk 1". — The assembly of the notables of Egypt will take the name of general couch."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I repeat your letter, Citizen General, by which you tell me that you are holding in prison the heads of the five villages that murdered a French boat; I hope you will make them pass under safe and proper escort to Cairo, to remain hostage."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I ask you to take steps to acquire the parts that would not belong to him. There is, beside the country house of Ibrahim-Bey, a house belonging to pilgrims:"
sourceTitle: To With A Chick'S Citovex, Cairo, 1798-10-09
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1." — There shall be two offices, each composed of two French interpreters and two Coptic writers, which shall be held with the Administrator of the Onances and shall be solely responsible for translating the cadastre which has been drawn up by the Coptics."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Every day, at few hours, the Chief Authorising Officer, the Financial Administrator and the Intendant General will go to the Chief General to hold a board of directors."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — Marine engineers shall carry out the work necessary to establish, at the head of the east pier, from the entrance to Ostend, a platform capable of containing five pieces of 36, and three of 36 at the head of the west pier."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The ceremonial you sent to the bishops is quite impassable in relation to our current customs; it will have to be replaced by a simpler one."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The regiments Watteville and Dillon, Swiss, have just been dismissed in Gibraltar and cross Spain in platoons of 30 to -40 men. Order them to stop at our borders to know what these men are, and to ensure that they do not slip into the Vendée."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Ask him if the leader of the 20th half-line brigade has arrived. Send from Fiance two battalion leaders to command the two free battalions of the country."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The 46th, 33rd and 51st are better, and have already received a part of the cloth of the year XI. By the state that you sent me, I see that in general the clothing is very retarded."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You must hold hands and gather your efforts to those of the Italians to activate and complete the conscription. I was satisfied with the feast of Marcngo."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Article 1. — The engineers of the marine works will have built, on the low-sea leash, to the right of the jetty of the east of the port of Boulogne, a platform in structure, capable of being armed with five large-calibre pieces and two mortars."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received, Citizen Consul, your letters from the 30 Messidor and 1st Thermidor. Since two days I have been in Brussels, I have not been out."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The season is too hot. I will give this trip to another circumstance. Bonaparte. Known, by AI. the Duke of Cambacérès. (In minutes at Arch. de l'Emp.) 414 "."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "It seemed a little tired of the road. All the Belgian ladies were presented today to my wife."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I think it would be useful to make the various communes aware that those who would like to obtain military effects would thereby be free from housing people of war;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The First Consul wishes that all that is relative to the diocese of Bordeaux be examined with the utmost care. The Archbishop seems to be a man of little mind and whose views are limited;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I send you, Citizen Minister, the report of the forest administration. It would be necessary that this extraordinary cut did not cost any money."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "The measures have been taken to ensure that there are at File d'Aix 5 or 600 men. I intend to be within eight or ten days in Paris."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive, Citizen Consul, your letters of the 10 and 11 Thermidor. The heats are no less strong here than in Paris."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please pass a note to M. de Souza, complaining about this violation. Regardless of this, an English privateer refuelled in the Tagus and stayed there for eight days."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I arrived this morning at six o'clock in Sedan, and, on the very repeated instances of the city of Reims, I decided to go there."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I have received, Citizen Minister, your letters of the 15th and 16th Thermidor. I have read with interest the new details on the insurrection of Ireland."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "You can tell them that they will be offered 25,000 men, 40,000 rifles and all the necessary artillery and ammunition; that the Government undertakes not to make peace with England unless Ireland's independence is established;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I am very much of his mind. All the news I receive from all sides tell me that our buildings are coming back to Spain, and even to the North. The heat is always very strong here"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I receive complaints that orders are not paid; and certainly, if an order is paid only eighty days after it has been issued, there is no more finance or services in the state."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "to derogate, for these buildings, only from the order of the 1st Messidor and not from any other law. To inform the Minister of Sweden of the order you give."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I send you, Citizen Minister, decisions on Swiss capitulation; send them by mail to General Ney, for I want this to be completed promptly."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "He therefore asks you to take information about the state of the old castle, and about the benefit that could be derived from it."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I will return the exhibits, Citizen Minister, with observations and notes on which should be supported a note in response to the Russian cabinet. You must assign to welcome the Russian officer very well and send him back to Mr."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I adopt, Citizen Minister, the numbers given to the various buildings. It is essential to draw up minutes, to see the year in which it was made, the room it bears, the name it had before, its draught, the length of its keel, etc."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Please have all the buildings in the fleet under construction prepared for the 15 Fructidor. Have it done with great care; understand what has been paid to each builder and what is owed to them."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I'm sending you back, Citizen Minister, the Madrid mail of 13. I'm surprised that we don't have any more news."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "General Caulaincourt, Citizen Minister, asked whether he could admit foreign officers to the 112th half-brigade. The answer must be negative; he must enter only Belgian officers."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "Citizen Admiral Bruix, I receive your letters of 27 and 2i) Fructidor. According to your calculation, you let me hope that all the pious ones will be placed at Red Fort at the 15 Vendemiary, and therefore the:2<> Vendemiary the fort can be armed."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "To the 11th, 13th and 19th regiments of dragons, who are in Hanover, to go to Maastricht, via the Prussian road. Let me know the day of their arrival in this place, to give them new orders."
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: "I ordered that three 36 pieces be placed on blinds such that they could shoot at the 45-degree angle, thus enabling them to throw G-inch shells and pellets at 2,000 and 2,300 toises;"
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858), Vols. VI–VII — public domain (French)
